findings.evidence: TauCeti/RingTheory/Valuation/Continuous/TopologicallyNilpotent.lean:110 `theorem IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent` in `namespace Valuation` (:76); used here at PowerBounded.lean:65 as `hv.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`.
findings.fix: Declare it as `Valuation.IsContinuous.le_one_of_isPowerBounded` (the namespace need not follow the directory; `Cont/Basic.lean:193` declares `IsContinuous.comap` from another tree), so the call site reads `hv.le_one_of_isPowerBounded hb hb0 ha`. Alternatively `TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.le_one`, dot notation on `ha`.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.Huber.le_one_of_isPowerBounded` is in the bare `Huber` namespace, so neither name nor namespace mentions the valuation whose value is `≤ 1`; it reads as a claim about power-bounded elements themselves. Its direct siblings — including the lemma this proof calls — are `Valuation.IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent` and `Valuation.IsContinuous.cofinalValue_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, which support `hv.…` dot notation.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/RankOne.lean:61-62 `nonempty_rankOne_iff_mulArchimedean … ↔ MulArchimedean (ValueGroup₀ (.ofClass v))`; the imported sibling file devotes a section to this distinction (TopologicallyNilpotent.lean:33 "## The value group, not the codomain").
findings.fix: Say the codomain `Γ₀` is archimedean, and title the file after the rank/height condition (e.g. "a continuous valuation with archimedean value monoid `Γ₀`") rather than "archimedean valuation"; if the value-group form is what is wanted, state the hypothesis on `ValueGroup₀ v`.
findings.issue: The hypothesis is `[MulArchimedean Γ₀]` on the codomain, but the module title, module docstring ("whose value monoid is archimedean", "Height one gives archimedean value group") and the declaration docstring ("with archimedean value monoid") name the value group `Γ_v`. Mathlib's cited equivalence yields `MulArchimedean (ValueGroup₀ v)`, which is not `MulArchimedean Γ₀`, so the stated recoverability from `Valuation.RankOne` does not hold as written. Separately, "archimedean valuation" in the title is standard terminology for an absolute value violating the ultrametric inequality — the opposite of what is meant here.

summary: The one new theorem is named out of its family: its siblings live in `Valuation.IsContinuous` for dot notation on the continuity hypothesis, while this one is a bare name in `TauCeti.Huber` with nothing identifying the valuation. The module and declaration docstrings also describe `[MulArchimedean Γ₀]` with terminology that names a different object.
